correctness.rationale: Derive the precise two-step flip affinity from the strong-dephasing transition rates. Strict concavity of F on the positive axis forces equality of absolute excluded-neighbor spin sums; all-plus assignments give equal degrees, and comparing degree-two spin-character coefficients forces identical other-neighbor sets whenever degree is at least three. Connected regular components are then cliques (degree at least three), cycles (degree two), edges or singletons. Explicit clique magnetization potentials and cycle Ising weights prove the converse. Strict positivity of rates gives unique stationary law and positive entropy production exactly when detailed balance fails. A standalone standard-library program tests 1,099 labelled graphs of order at most five and 608 detailed-balance equations on larger reversible examples; these are diagnostics, not a replacement for the proof.

value.rationale: The motivating strong-dephasing sampler has equilibrium on a periodic chain but nonequilibrium circulation on a square lattice. The exact graph topology criterion resolves the natural design question across all finite simple graphs and shows a surprising boundary: deleting one cycle edge or adding a pendant vertex can turn equilibrium into irreversible steady current, whereas cliques remain reversible despite nonzero many-body Gibbs couplings. The classification determines when entropy-producing currents must exist, without assuming particular graph sizes or estimating unknown stationary measures.
